content.text: {"changes":[{"type":"modified","heading":"Global economic, political, financial and societal events or conditions could result in a material and adverse impact on our overall business and results of operations.","description":"A new bullet was added to the adverse economic trends list identifying uncertain global trade policies and government actions related to tariffs as a risk to the business and stakeholder relationships.","quote":"•Uncertain global trade policies and related government actions (including those related to tariffs), which could have an adverse impact on our business (including with respect to consumer and business spending) and relationships with stakeholders"},{"type":"modified","heading":"Adverse currency fluctuations and foreign exchange controls could negatively impact our results of operations.","description":"The share of revenue generated from activities outside the U.S. increased from approximately 70% in 2024 to approximately 71% in 2025.","quote":"During 2025, approximately 71% of our revenue was generated from activities outside the U.S., which could be transacted in a non-functional currency."},{"type":"modified","heading":"Negative brand perception may materially and adversely affect our overall business.","description":"A new sentence was added stating that actions the company or its customers take (or are perceived to take) related to high-risk merchant industries could be viewed negatively and result in threats or other retaliatory actions.","quote":"Additionally, we or our customers could take (or be perceived to take) actions related to these industries, which could be viewed negatively and result in threats or other retaliatory actions."},{"type":"modified","heading":"Environmental, social and governance matters and related stakeholder reaction may impact our reputation, increase legal exposure and/or have other business impacts, which could adversely affect our overall business and/or results of operations.","description":"The description of ESG initiatives was changed from helping everyone participate \"equitably\" in the digital economy and creating a workplace \"that provides equal opportunities for all of our employees\" to participating in the digital economy and a workplace \"where everyone has the opportunity to succeed,\" and the trigger for negative stakeholder views was expanded from disclosures viewed as \"inaccurate\" to \"inaccurate or unlawful.\"","quote":"These matters include initiatives to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, help everyone participate in the digital economy and create a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to succeed. Consumers, investors, employees and other stakeholders are increasingly focused on these impacts. To the extent any of our disclosures, public statements and metrics about these matters are subsequently viewed as inaccurate or unlawful, or we are unable to execute on these initiatives, we may be viewed negatively by stakeholders concerned about these matters."},{"type":"modified","heading":"We may not be able to attract and retain a highly qualified workforce, or maintain our corporate culture, which could harm our overall business and results of operations.","description":"The workforce-expectations paragraph dropped the references to employees having different career motivations (such as project-based or gig work rather than linear career paths) and to a negative impact on the company's ability to innovate; the competitive labor market description was also narrowed from \"technology and other areas that are important to the growth of our business\" to \"emerging technologies.\"","quote":"As our workforce composition continues to change, our employees may have different expectations with respect to flexibility and well-being support. Additionally, employees may require different levels of support as to re-skilling and upskilling in order to adapt to advancements in our industry and changes in technology. Further, certain current and prospective employees may have expectations as to positions we take on environmental, social and governance matters. To the extent we are unable to effectively meet and/or balance these different expectations and needs, we could experience a negative impact to the quality of our corporate culture, the productivity of our workforce and our ability to attract and retain talent."},{"type":"modified","heading":"Our efforts to enter into acquisitions, strategic investments or new businesses could be impacted or prevented by regulatory scrutiny and could otherwise result in issues that could disrupt our business and harm our results of operations or reputation.","description":"The consequence of inherited litigation risk was narrowed by deleting the prior statement that it may \"impact our ability to successfully finance that business,\" leaving only increased post-acquisition costs of operations.","quote":"Furthermore, we have inherited and may in the future inherit litigation risk which has or may increase our post-acquisition costs of operations."},{"type":"modified","heading":"Our role as guarantor, as well as other contractual obligations and discretionary actions, expose us to risk of loss or illiquidity.","description":"The bank failure reference was broadened from failures \"in recent years in the U.S.\" to \"in recent years,\" and the general statement that jurisdictions could require extension of the company's guarantee was replaced with a specific new Brazilian regulation requiring PSOs (including Mastercard and Visa) to extend responsibility for the financial and settlement integrity of payments to merchants, with the stated impact expanded to cost of operations and financial condition.","quote":"The occurrence of bank failures, such as those seen in recent years, could increase the potential for such losses. Concurrent settlement failures of more than one of our larger customers or of several smaller customers either on a given day or over a condensed period of time may exceed our available resources. In addition, Brazil recently enacted regulation requiring PSOs in Brazil (including Mastercard and Visa) to extend their responsibility for the financial and settlement integrity of payments to merchants. As we continue to be subject to increased regulation across the globe, more jurisdictions may enact similar approaches from time to time. Any such changes could increase complexity and may impact our cost of operations and financial condition."},{"type":"modified","heading":"Mastercard Foundation’s substantial stock ownership, and restrictions on its sales, may impact corporate actions or acquisition proposals favorable to, or favored by, the other public stockholders.","description":"The disclosed Mastercard Foundation ownership changed from a specific approximately 9.4% of general voting power as of December 31, 2024 to a general statement of greater than 5% of general voting power with no measurement date.","quote":"Mastercard Foundation owns shares of our Class A common stock representing greater than 5% of our general voting power."}]}
